title: Stalk of the compactly supported direct image
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\pi:E\to B$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(E,\Lambda)$, and let
$\bar b\to B$ be a geometric
point with the fiber $E_{\bar b}$. The canonical comparison

$$
(R\pi_!K)_{\bar b}\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;R\Gamma_c(E_{\bar b},K|_{E_{\bar b}})
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text: By [def-pur-conventions], $E$ and $B$ are finite-type $k$-schemes and $\pi$ is a separated finite-type $k$-morphism. Form the cartesian compact-support square [def-cbc-compact-support-square] with $g=\bar b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$, $X'=E_{\bar b}=E\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $f'=\pi_{\bar b}:E_{\bar b}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $g'=i_{\bar b}:E_{\bar b}\to E$; by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] $\pi_{\bar b}$ is separated of finite type, so $E_{\bar b}$ is a finite-type $\Omega$-scheme, and $\ell$ is invertible in $\Omega\supseteq k$. Fix a compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $\pi$ as supplied by [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]; its base change $c'=(j',p')$ is a compactification of $\pi_{\bar b}$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square], so $R(\pi_{\bar b})_!$ is the compact-support direct image of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] over the field $K_0=\Omega$ (and its coefficient forms). The two sides of the display are read as follows: $K|_{E_{\bar b}}=Li_{\bar b}^*K$ is the derived pullback of the coefficient stage [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and $R\Gamma_c(E_{\bar b},K|_{E_{\bar b}})$ is $R(\pi_{\bar b})_!(K|_{E_{\bar b}})$ on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The stalk $(R\pi_!K)_{\bar b}$ is the filtered-neighborhood stalk of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] (at finite level on the etale witness, on each cohomology sheaf). By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], applied to $f=\bar b$ and the tautological geometric point $\mathrm{id}$ of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, it is the stalk of $\bar b^{-1}R\pi_!K$ at that point. Since $\Omega$ is separably closed, an etale $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and a lift of $\mathrm{id}$ picks one copy, so $(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,\mathrm{id})$ is final among pointed etale neighbourhoods and that stalk is the value on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. At the integral and field stages the stalk is likewise the stage pullback $L\bar b^*R\pi_!K$ on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. So in every stage the displayed comparison is the compact-support exchange $L\bar b^*R\pi_!K\to R(\pi_{\bar b})_!Li_{\bar b}^*K$ of this square, read on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and it suffices to show that this exchange is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof paragraph, first sentence and compactification setup

proof.text: At finite level $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $D^b_c(E,A_{E,n})$ is the intrinsic bounded constructible pro-etale category, so $K$ has a bounded constructible etale-origin witness $(L,\alpha)$ by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] (ii). Apply [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] ($\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ finite, $\pi$ separated of finite type, $g=\bar b$ arbitrary, compactification $c$ given) to the square of Step 1. Its canonical exchange is an isomorphism $\bar b^{-1}R\pi_!K\simeq R(\pi_{\bar b})_!\,i_{\bar b}^{-1}K$, and $i_{\bar b}^{-1}K$ carries the witness $(i_{\bar b}^{-1}L,i_{\bar b}^{-1}\alpha)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Taking the value on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ as in Step 1 gives the comparison with $R\Gamma_c(E_{\bar b},K|_{E_{\bar b}})$. This is the route of the source: after writing $R\pi_!=Rp_*j_!$, the proper factor is the geometric-fibre formula [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] applied to $p$ and the witness $j_!L$, and the open factor is the extension-by-zero part of the same exchange.

source.place: Proof paragraph, compatibility of geometric stalks with compact-support functors and proper direct image

proof.text:
Let $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$. The four schemes $E,B,E_{\bar b},\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ are of finite type over the field $k$ or $\Omega$, hence noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and finite-dimensional [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], and $\ell$ is invertible on them. In particular every open subscheme of $E$ is quasi-compact, so $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], over each of them the category $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] is the category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], with the same completed ring sheaf and reductions. So $K$ is derived $\varpi_E$-complete and its reductions $K_n$ carry compatible etale-origin witnesses. Apply [thm-cbc-complete-proetale] with $(A,I)=(\mathcal O_E,(\varpi_E))$ to the square of Step 1 and to $c$: the completed exchange $L\bar b^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rp_*j_!K\to Rp'_*j'_!Li^*_{\bar b,\mathrm{comp}}K$ is an isomorphism. Its ends are those of Step 1.

(a) Pullbacks: the integral pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nLf_n^*(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$. [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] defines $Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ as $R\lim$ of the strict tower whose $n$-th evaluation is $Lf_n^*K_n$. These are the derived limit of the same tower.

(b) Direct images: by [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] (identity square of the quasi-compact $j$), $j_!K$ is complete, so its completion unit identifies it with $J^c_jK$. Transport through the restriction-of-scalars equivalence on complete objects of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Then [lem-sf-cbc-extension-zero-completion] gives $J^c_jK\cong R\lim(j_!K_n)_n$ with the reduction transitions, and [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] gives $Rp_*R\lim\cong R\lim Rp_*^{\mathrm{Tow}}$. Hence $Rp_*j_!K\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}j_!K_n$, which is $R\pi_!K$ of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] for the compactification $c$. The same argument applies to $\pi_{\bar b}$, $c'$ and the complete object $Li^*_{\bar b,\mathrm{comp}}K$.

Under these identifications the isomorphism of [thm-cbc-complete-proetale] is the integral comparison of Step 1. Its value on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ gives the displayed isomorphism at integral coefficients.

source.place: Proof paragraph, coefficient-tower interpretation (transport of the compactification exchange to integral coefficients per def-pur-conventions)

proof.text:
Let $\Lambda=E$, the coefficient field (not the scheme $E$). Over the four schemes of Step 3 the integral categories agree by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. So the raw rationalizations of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] are one category: the same objects and $\operatorname{Hom}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$. By [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] the rational $R\pi_!$ is the integral one on objects, and the rational pullback is formed on integral representatives. By the uniqueness clause of [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] these are the $E$-linear extensions used in [thm-cbc-finite-extension], and the rational exchange is the extension of the integral exchange of Step 3. The hypotheses of [thm-cbc-finite-extension] hold: all four schemes are noetherian, finite-dimensional and have $\ell$ invertible (Step 3), $\pi$ is separated of finite type, and $g=\bar b$ is arbitrary. So $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,E}(K)$ is an isomorphism for every $K\in D^b_c(E,E)=D^b_{ctf}(E,E)$, and its value on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is the displayed comparison.

Let $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. By [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], $D^b_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ is the finite-stage pair category formed with the rational stages above and their scalar extensions. With the stage categories identified and the scalar extensions compared by [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport], it is the category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. On an object $(E',K_{E'})$, $R\pi_!(E',K_{E'})=(E',R\pi_!K_{E'})$ is the value of the descended functor of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors]. [thm-cbc-qbar] (finite-stage hypotheses as just checked) shows that the descended exchange is an isomorphism. After a finite overfield $M$ it is represented by the isomorphism of [thm-cbc-finite-extension] for $T_{M/E'}K_{E'}$, independently of $E'$, $M$ and the representative. Its value on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is the displayed comparison.

source.place: Proof paragraph, coefficient transports (per def-pur-conventions, transport section)

proof.text: All comparisons used above are the canonical compactification, witness, stalk, and coefficient-transport maps, so their composite is the displayed canonical map. Naturality in $K$ follows from naturality of each cited exchange and stalk comparison. Edge cases: for an empty fibre both sides are $0$; for $K=0$ both sides are $0$; for $\pi=\mathrm{id}$ the compactification is $(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$ and both sides are $K_{\bar b}$; for $B=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $\bar b=\mathrm{id}$ the square is the identity square and the exchange is the identity.

split_report.summary: Expanded the imported compactification argument into five steps. Step 1 fixes the base-changed compactification and identifies the stalk as the geometric-point inverse-image fibre. Step 2 applies finite-level pro-etale compact-support base change to an etale-origin witness and identifies the proper fibre term with the geometric-fibre formula. Steps 3 and 4 spell out the integral, rational, and common-stage coefficient transports using the completed tower realization, finite-extension base change, and Qbar descent. Step 5 records canonicality, naturality, and edge cases. No new nodes were needed; every cited statement was checked against its recorded hypotheses. Maintainer review (2026-10-18): Steps 1, 3 and 4 were repaired. Step 1 now defines the fibre square, $R\Gamma_c$ and the stalk reading. Step 3 now cites the identification of the integral categories, the completeness of $j_!$, the extension-by-zero limit presentation and the direct-image limit comparison that match the completed exchange with the tower definition of $R\pi_!$. Step 4 now cites the identification of the purity rational and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ categories with the proper-base-change ones before applying thm-cbc-finite-extension and thm-cbc-qbar.
